pc_gate_ledger_notes.text: PIN. The post/comment `text` and the profile `bio`/`location` are concrete strings (the MessageRenderer gsub pipeline needs a real String), pinned WITH a recorded decision family over everything the app actually branches on inside them: `_text_nil`, `_text_has_mention`, `_mention_inline_name`, `_text_has_dlink`, `_text_dlink_is_post` and the SYM_PARAM_dlink_guid_* parameter the link family feeds to `Post.exists?`. The COLUMN itself is never compared; its branch-relevant content is. Same entry shape as conversations_index's `text` pin.
pc_gate_ledger_notes.bio: PIN — see `text`; the profile display family is `_disp_has_dlink` / `_disp_dlink_is_post` / SYM_PARAM_disp_dlink_guid_*.
pc_gate_ledger_notes.target_type: PIN (derived, both values realised). `notifications.target_type` is never COMPARED by the endpoint: it is dispatched on (`owner[foreign_type].constantize` in BelongsToPolymorphicAssociation#klass) and the app's own branch is on the resulting CLASS (`posts_helper.rb:9 post.is_a?(Photo)`). Its value is a function of the RECORDED decision `<rep>_target_is_photo` over the real commentable set {Post, Photo} (adversary W2 / N-2), so both values occur in the corpus and no subclass family is foreclosed. REACHABILITY (T-g): a value outside {Post, Photo} is expressible in the database (`notifications.target_type` is a plain string with no CHECK) but not through the app — `comment_on_post.rb:22`/`also_commented.rb:23` pass `comment.commentable`, and `Diaspora::Commentable` is included only by Post and Photo. An out-of-tree value makes `owner[foreign_type].constantize` raise NameError at the preload step, truncating the request after the notifications read — again a strict PREFIX of the modelled statement set.
pc_gate_ledger_notes.mentions_container_type: PIN (derived, both values realised). Determined in the app by the notification's STI type (MentionedInPost -> Post, MentionedInComment -> Comment), i.e. by the recorded SYM_NOTE_TYPE_PROFILE dispatch; both values occur in the corpus. It appears in notes only as the literal of the REAL association scope (`mentions.mentions_container_type = 'Post'`).
pc_gate_ledger_notes.commentable_type: PIN (derived, both values realised). Same mechanism as target_type: Comment#commentable is polymorphic over {Post, Photo} and the value follows `<rep>_target_is_photo`.
pc_gate_ledger_notes.taggable_type: PIN (not free). `taggings.taggable_type = 'Profile'` is the literal in the REAL acts_as_taggable scope of `profile.tags`; a Profile is the only taggable this endpoint renders.
pc_gate_ledger_notes._params_pins:
Request PARAMETERS (not columns, listed for completeness).

`params[:type]` (notifications_controller.rb:28) — a Hash#eql? wall, driven as the `*_typed` VARIANTS instead of as a symbolic value. NEUTRALITY: a key OUTSIDE `types` falls through `types.has_key?` to exactly the untyped path, and each key INSIDE it differs only in the literal bound into `conditions[:type]`, which the note renders as a bind. So the pin costs no shape and no arm.

`params[:page]` (:32) — REWRITTEN 2026-09-01 (C7). The previous entry said its "branch-relevant effect ... IS explored, as the `rows` length decision". That reason is FALSE and is withdrawn: `WillPaginate::Collection.create` -> `Collection#initialize` -> `WillPaginate::PageNumber(page)` -> `PageNumber#initialize` calls `Integer(value)` and raises RangeError when `value < 1` (ArgumentError when non-numeric), tagged `WillPaginate::InvalidPage`, which the gem's railtie maps to HTTP 404 (will_paginate-3.3.0 page_number.rb:14-23, railtie.rb:48-50). The `rows` length decision cannot express that terminal.
The pin nonetheless HOLDS, on a PREFIX argument that names its step: `Notification.where(conditions).count` is an ARGUMENT to `Collection.create`, so it is evaluated BEFORE `PageNumber#initialize` can raise. An invalid-page request therefore issues exactly {the principal SELECT, the notifications COUNT} and nothing else — a strict PREFIX of the statement set every modelled run already carries, so the pin costs the policy no SHAPE. Stated explicitly, because a prefix argument justifies the STATEMENTS and not the OUTCOME: the 404 terminal itself is NOT modelled and is NOT claimed to be.

`params[:per_page]` (:33) — `@per_page = per_page.to_i`, no validation anywhere in `Collection#initialize`. It moves only the LIMIT/OFFSET binds, which every note wildcards; at 0 it yields the empty page, which is already the modelled `rows == 0` cardinality. Pinned at 25.
pc_gate_ledger_notes._belongs_to_pin_narrowed: Cycle 6 (B-4): the blanket 'every belongs_to is pinned found' pin is WITHDRAWN. It is now conditional on the FK column being backed by a real foreign key (ConcolicTargets::FK_BACKED_COLUMNS, transcribed from db/schema.rb's add_foreign_key list). belongs_to over an FK-LESS column carries a LIVE not-found decision on BOTH the find_target path and the preload path, with the same predicate name: `mentions.person_id`, `photos.status_message_guid`, `photos.author_id`, `notifications.recipient_id`, `notifications.target_id`.
pc_gate_ledger_notes.language_MODELLED: GATE, cycle 6 (T-f / M-5). `users.language` was a PIN with the argument 'set_locale is a before_action this runner does not dispatch'. That is a SCOPE statement, not a reachability argument, and the coordinator's M-5 shows the state is real: the column is NOT NULL, has no CHECK and is not validated against the shipped locale set, so a locale dropped by an upgrade survives in the row and `I18n.locale = current_user.language` raises `I18n::InvalidLocale` BEFORE the action body — one statement (the Devise principal load), then 500. It is now MODELLED: `run_dse.rb` dispatches the REAL `set_locale`, and the User representative carries the decision `<rep>_language_available` (targets.rb) that chooses an available locale or a dropped one. The raise is the app's own.
pc_gate_ledger_notes.type_STI_reachability: T-g / M-6 — reachability argument for the STI enumeration (the coordinator's requirement). `notifications.type` is a placeholder column: NOT NULL, no CHECK, no validation, so an out-of-tree value is expressible in the DATABASE. It is NOT expressible through the application: every row is created by `NotificationService#notify` -> `Notifications::<Klass>.notify` (notification_service.rb:8-9 wires the type set) and `Notification.create` is never called with a free-form type. So an out-of-tree value can only arrive as LEGACY / IMPORTED / downgraded data — the same provenance as the `PrivateMessage` pin (W3). CONSEQUENCE, written down rather than assumed harmless: at materialization `ActiveRecord::Inheritance#find_sti_class` raises `ActiveRecord::SubclassNotFound` and the request truncates, so its statement set is `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notifications …` plus `SELECT notifications.* … ORDER BY updated_at desc LIMIT ? OFFSET ?` and NOTHING ELSE — a strict PREFIX of the statement set every corpus run already carries. The pin therefore costs the policy no shape. The Photo case the adversary found (N-2) was the SAME class on `target_type` and is NOT pinned: it is the recorded decision `_target_is_photo` over {Post, Photo}, the values `Notifications::CommentOnPost`/`AlsoCommented` can really produce.
pc_gate_ledger_notes._C7_layout_unpinned: C7 (2026-09-01) — `NotificationsController.layout(false)` WITHDRAWN from run_dse.rb AND from all six concrete manifests. It was never a neutrality pin; it was a scope decision asserting the site chrome was "unrelated to this endpoint's query shape", and the measurement refutes it: real layout 42 statements vs 25 pinned on html, 35 vs 21 on mobile, with SEVEN shapes absent from the whole 39 956-dump pinned corpus (aspects by user_id; services; tags INNER JOIN tag_followings; two roles existence reads; COUNT(*) contacts; SUM(conversation_visibilities.unread)). Because the same pin sat in the ground-truth manifests, no judge could see any of it — parity between a rig and its own ground truth is a tautology, not evidence (DISCIPLINE 14). These reads are ENDPOINT material: they are issued inside the action's own request while rendering its response, and do not belong to the shared auth boundary (DISCIPLINE 15). The sprockets gap that originally justified the pin is real and is closed by emptying the asset resolvers (ActionView::Base.resolve_assets_with = []), as conversations_index did for C-12/INSTR-8.
pc_gate_ledger_notes._C7_render_safe_display_columns: C7 (2026-09-01) — NOT A PIN, recorded here so nobody mistakes it for one. With the layout un-pinned, `_drawer.mobile.haml` feeds `aspect.name` / `tag.name` into `link_to` -> `unwrapped_html_escape` -> `tidy_bytes` -> `String#scrub`, which the shared runtime does not support on SymbolicString (src/ruby_runtime/string.rb:359) — a RIG-class NotImplementedError that `rig_crash_census` correctly fails on. targets.rb now upgrades those columns to `TypeLinkedString` (a ConcreteSymbolicString subclass that records `==` / `!=`), so they are render-safe AND still PC-VISIBLE: Rule G's gate/pin partition is unchanged and `pc_visibility_audit --gate` can still see any compare the app makes. The runtime gap is REPORTED, not patched; src/ is untouched.
pc_gate_ledger_notes._C7_before_action_chain: C7 (2026-09-01) — the rig now dispatches the WHOLE before_action chain via Rails' own `run_callbacks(:process_action)`, not one hand-picked filter. Previously only `set_locale` ran, so `gon_set_current_user` never built the `UserPresenter` and its serialisation reads (`SELECT "services".* WHERE user_id`, `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "contacts" WHERE user_id AND receiving`) had no call site at all — 0 events over 114 dumps even AFTER the layout pin was withdrawn. A pin can hide a shape; a missing dispatch path hides the reason the shape exists. The chain is read from the controller, never from a list copied into the runner (DISCIPLINE 14). First attempt iterated `_process_action_callbacks` by name and ignored :if/:unless, invoking `configure_permitted_parameters` (guarded by `devise_controller?`, false here) 113 times in a 116-dump round; `run_callbacks` evaluates every condition, runs after/around callbacks and honours a halted chain. Mobile now reaches `:mobile` through the app's own `mobile_switch` filter rather than the rig setting the format, so the rig and the concrete manifests agree by taking the SAME CODE PATH instead of by being configured alike.
pc_gate_ledger_notes._C7_reload_unreachable: C7 (2026-09-01) — `ActiveRecord::Base#reload` (boundary harvest B-1) is UNREACHABLE on this endpoint after the wall relocation, and that is correct, not a regression. `Person#fix_profile` was its only route here; declaring `fix_profile` a target skips `Discovery.new`, `fetch_and_save` AND `reload` together. The declaration stays; the boundary exercise census will report it 0-invoked. The relocation also DELETES 1 906 `reload` statements the pre-repair corpus emitted on an arm where the application never reaches `reload` at all (the DiscoveryError precedes it) — so the repair removes over-approximation as well as adding truth. Verified on the repaired model: 144-dump smoke, 5 `WALL Person#fix_profile` events, 0 reload events.
pc_gate_ledger_notes._C7_boundary_changes_reported:
C7 (2026-09-01) — FOUR shared-boundary defects found on this endpoint, all REPORTED under Rule T3 and worked around batch-locally; none patched in the shared file.
1. `Gon::ControllerHelpers#gon` — the stub's `push` is a no-op outside AUTH_CHAIN, and its own comment gives the reason as the `layout(false)` decision this cycle withdrew. Already RULED withdrawn in TARGET_FUNCTIONS §3 (2026-08-30, C-10/C-12) but NOT applied to `concolic_targets.rb`, so this corpus was still running the swallowing stub. Worked around by prepending the gem's real four-line body to NotificationsController.
2. `Calculations#sum` renders a ROW projection where the app issues `SELECT SUM(col)`. First corpus in the project to invoke `sum` at all.
3. `Relation#size` renders a ROW projection where the app issues `SELECT COUNT(*)`. `size` is 0-invoked on comments_index and conversations_index; this is the first corpus that could see it. It produced BOTH unexplained multiplicity rows of this cycle (the mobile badge is read twice).
4. `SingularAssociation#find_target` has no loaded-target memo, so a has_one read twice in one request re-issues. T-z/C-13 extended from CollectionProxy to singular associations. Measured: 86 of 4 954 dumps, and — comparing notes by EXACT text with BIND IDENTITY INCLUDED — all 86 are the same statement with the same bind, 0 are two different owners.
pc_gate_ledger_notes._C7_INSTR9_one_request_per_process: C7 (2026-09-01), INSTR-9 — GROUND TRUTH MUST BE ONE REQUEST PER PROCESS. A second request in the same process under-reports its statements, and `Rails.application.executor.wrap` does NOT fix it. Mechanism: `GonHelper#gon_load_contact` (gon_helper.rb:4-8) accumulates into the PROCESS-level `Gon.preloads[:contacts]` and SKIPS building the presenter when a contact with the same person_id is already stored, so `ContactPresenter#full_hash_with_person`'s reads (aspect_memberships, aspects by id, blocks, tags INNER JOIN taggings) never fire again. Established by running the same four scenarios in BOTH orders: 4 shapes 'lost' forward, 0 reversed — an order effect, not an executor effect. All six concrete manifests now drive exactly one request per process (CC_REQ). Rebuilt ground truth: 14 processes, 334 statements, 38 distinct shapes; per-process shape counts auth req0 27, req1 19, req2 15, req3 10.

h6_answered.reason: SCOPE-CONSTANT LITERAL vs BOUND value. `Notification.unread` puts `unread = true` INTO the relation, and Arel#to_sql — which sql_for renders from — inlines it, while the real statement logs `"notifications"."unread" = ?`. Same tables, same predicate columns, same value; note_fidelity_audit scores every one EXACT and statement_note_lint is green. Only H6's byte-shape compare separates `= true` from `= ?`, because `true` is a bare word its normalizer does not wildcard.

KEY-SET ARITY, not a different family. Since DISCIPLINE §13 Rule D a preload renders one bind per row actually loaded; this model's MANY is 3 (4 for a preloaded association) while the concrete runs' pages hold 2, 4, 5 and 25 rows, so `IN (@, @, @)` never matches `IN (@, @)` byte-for-byte. Same tables, same predicate column, same bulk operator: note_fidelity_audit (which wildcards the bind list) scores these EXACT, and cardinality_consistency_audit confirms each agrees with its run's own `len > 1` decision. Widening the arity further would mean inventing rows the corpus does not have.
